page: Amazon Web Services c8in.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server type built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, with two hardware threads per physical core. The platform supplies 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio typical of compute-intensive infrastructure. The configuration contains no discrete GPU accelerators.

A prominent capability of the instance is its network interface, which provides a 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. However, the hardware specification includes no bundled local storage volumes, requiring all persistent storage and operational filesystems to depend entirely on external network-attached services such as Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS). Operating without local disks necessitates careful planning for I/O operations, though the massive 300 Gbps network capacity mitigates network bottlenecking during heavy storage and inter-node communication.

From a cost-efficiency and performance perspective, c8in.48xlarge provides high resource density by packing 192 compute threads and high network bandwidth into a single instance footprint. It is suited for workloads that demand substantial processor parallelization coupled with extreme network throughput, such as clustered distributed computing, network-intensive batch processing, scientific simulations, and large-scale media processing pipelines.
